grade.rationale: The reply matches the reference on the key point: Both sends both parts in one message and the client decides, so the QR attachment is the safety net. It also says major providers usually render HTML, with the risk coming from the recipient's settings. It omits alt text and the Outlook CID caveat, but adds a sensible plain-text fallback link, and it has no errors.

grade.material_error_what: Points the customer toward project placement and moving items between projects as the cause and fix. Moving items again could also revoke sharing and make things worse. The reply never mentions the env var or caller policy.

grade.material_error_what: Recommends human-in-the-loop approval as the way to get deterministic tool control. That feature gates tool execution on human approval and does not force the model to call a tool or stop it from hallucinating; for an automated Instagram/Facebook chatbot it is impractical. It also suggests streaming as a timeout fix, which doesn't apply to Instagram/Facebook webhook triggers. The reply never mentions the reference's key step: switch to a top-tier model and add guard clauses and an output validator.

It names three routes (GitHub, n8n support, forum) rather than one, offers nothing to do in the meantime, and includes a Cloud/billing suggestion that doesn't fit a TrueNAS customer. grade.material_error_what: Steps 1-3 point the customer at the wrong causes: switching to Append or Update Row, and checking for gaps/breaks in the sheet layout. The real cause is a non-atomic append under concurrent requests. Append or Update Row would not stop the race and would need a matching column. The only relevant idea, queueing writes, is vague and has no concrete implementation (no Wait node, no Postgres queue).

support.claim: n8n warns that the append endpoint can misplace data when the sheet has gaps or breaks

Concurrent webhook executions writing to Sheets at once cause the lost rows

grade.rationale: The reply correctly names concurrent writes as the likely cause and mentions queueing in step 4, which is in the direction of the reference fix. But it leads with misdirecting advice (switch to Append or Update Row, check sheet gaps) based on a misapplied docs passage, and the queueing suggestion has no concrete steps such as a Wait node with random delay or a Postgres queue. The customer would likely waste time and come back.
